extracted.intended_audience: care provider facilities, ORR staff, legal advocates, state/local child welfare agencies, service providers, and public commenters on the NPRM
extracted.subtask_description: A Department of Health and Human Services/ORR notice of proposed rulemaking proposing to codify standards and procedures for the placement, care, services, and administrative review related to unaccompanied children in ORR custody, and instructions for public participation in the rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 410.1000—Scope of This Part
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines the scope of the proposed part establishing policies and requirements for placement, care, and services provided to unaccompanied children referred to ORR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States that proposed requirements apply to all care provider facilities (standard and non-standard programs) unless otherwise specified; codifies ORR policies and FSA substantive protections as they pertain to ORR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 410.1001—Definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides definitions of terms relevant to the criteria and requirements in the proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies terms such as 'restrictive placement', 'standard program', 'care provider facility types', and uses statutory definitions (e.g., HSA definition of 'unaccompanied child').

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 410.1002—ORR Care and Placement of Unaccompanied Children
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR's responsibilities for coordinating and implementing care and placement of unaccompanied children in Federal custody by reason of immigration status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR must place children in the least restrictive setting appropriate to age and needs, consider danger to self/community and risk of flight, apply child welfare principles, and oversee provider infrastructure and personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 410.1003—General Principles That Apply to the Care and Placement of Unaccompanied Children
rubrics_metrics.description: Articulates general principles governing care and placement decisions (best interests, least restrictive setting, child welfare principles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR considers each child's unique situation and the best interests of the child when making placement, clinical, case management, and release decisions; prioritizes safety, well-being, and public transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 410.1004—ORR Custody of Unaccompanied Children
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishes that unaccompanied children not released remain in ORR legal custody and may be transferred or released only under ORR authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes custody-transfer responsibilities (e.g., transfers from DHS) and limits on release authority; notes procedures for children who turn 18 while in ORR care (transfer to DHS for custody determination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart B—Purpose and Process for Placement After Referral (Section 410.1100–410.1101)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets out the purpose of placement subpart and the process for placement of an unaccompanied child after referral from another Federal agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes statutory timeframes and coordination (e.g., TVPRA 48/72-hour notifications/transfers), required notifications to ORR, and expectations for prompt placement in the least restrictive appropriate setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 410.1102—Care Provider Facility Types
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorizes facility types (standard programs, secure facilities, heightened supervision facilities, RTCs, emergency/influx facilities) and their applicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different facility types have different standards and placement criteria; non-standard programs are identified and addressed separately when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 410.1103—Considerations Generally Applicable to the Placement of an Unaccompanied Child
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists considerations ORR must take into account for placement decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes danger to self, danger to community, risk of flight, child's age/special needs, best interests, child welfare principles, and privacy protections when consulting with juvenile justice and other agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 410.1104—Placement of an Unaccompanied Child in a Standard Program That Is Not Restrictive
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria and expectations for placement of children in standard, non-restrictive programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard programs must meet minimum standards and provide services (education, healthcare, recreation, mental health, legal access) appropriate to the child's needs; ORR prioritizes non-restrictive placements when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 410.1105—Criteria for Placing an Unaccompanied Child in a Restrictive Placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies when placement in restrictive settings (secure, heightened supervision, RTC) is permitted and the criteria required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restrictive placements are limited to circumstances where less restrictive settings are not appropriate given safety, treatment needs, or other risks; includes requirements for periodic review of restrictive placements (e.g., 30-day and 45-day reviews).

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 410.1106—Unaccompanied Children Who Need Particular Services and Treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses placement and services for children with specialized clinical, mental health, or other treatment needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires placement decisions to consider individualized treatment needs and to place children in settings capable of delivering required services; references policies for children with disabilities and mental health needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 410.1107—Considerations When Determining Whether an Unaccompanied Child Is a Runaway Risk for Purposes of Placement Decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for assessing runaway risk when making placement decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR evaluates indicators of flight risk and balances those against least restrictive setting principles; runaway-risk determinations inform placement but do not necessarily dictate release decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 410.1108—Placement and Services for Children of Unaccompanied Children
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses placement and services when an unaccompanied child has dependents (children of unaccompanied children).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures consideration of family integrity and appropriate placement/services for dependent children consistent with applicable statutes and child welfare standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 410.1109—Required Notice of Legal Rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires that unaccompanied children receive required notices of legal rights while in ORR care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes explanations of availability of legal assistance, right to be represented (described as a 'privilege' under statute), bond-hearing information, and other procedural rights consistent with FSA and TVPRA obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart C—Purpose of Releasing an Unaccompanied Child From ORR Custody (Section 410.1200)
rubrics_metrics.description: States the purpose of subpart addressing release processes and policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Codifies policies and procedures for release to vetted sponsors and related safeguards to ensure child safety and appearance at proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 410.1201—Sponsors to Whom ORR Releases an Unaccompanied Child
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishes the order of priority and types of sponsors to whom ORR may release a child (parent, legal guardian, adult relative, other adult designated by parent/guardian).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When no sponsor is available, placement at licensed care provider facility; ORR implements safety and suitability assessments for proposed sponsors consistent with TVPRA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 410.1202—Sponsor Suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria and procedures for determining whether a proposed sponsor is suitable for release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes background checks, safety and suitability assessments, documentation requirements, and limitations on release based on findings; addresses privacy protections and information sharing limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 410.1203—Release Approval Process
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures ORR uses to approve release of an unaccompanied child to a sponsor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies multi-step approval including verification, home-study triggers, and authority to deny release if sponsor is unsuitable; outlines potential discretionary release to programs like Unaccompanied Refugee Minors Program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 410.1204—Home Studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Circumstances requiring home studies and what home studies must assess when a non-relative or certain sponsors seek to sponsor a child.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Home study requirements apply to non-relative sponsors in specified circumstances (multiple children, prior sponsorship, young children under 12); ORR may conduct follow-up services per statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 410.1205—Release Decisions; Denial of Release to a Sponsor
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and reasons for denying release to a proposed sponsor and documentation of release decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR may deny release when sponsor is unsuitable or placement would not be in child's best interests; denials must be documented and are subject to appeal provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 410.1206—Appeals of Release Denials
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures allowing review/appeal of ORR release denial decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides for administrative review mechanisms; describes timelines and procedural safeguards for contested release decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 410.1207—Ninety (90)-Day Review of Pending Release Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires periodic (90-day) review of pending release applications to ensure timely processing and consideration of children awaiting release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures ORR reviews and updates status of prolonged pending release cases; clarifies review triggers and responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 410.1208—ORR's Discretion To Release an Unaccompanied Child to the Unaccompanied Refugee Minors Program
rubrics_metrics.description: Allows ORR discretion to place children into the Unaccompanied Refugee Minors Program as an alternative release option.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes ORR authority and process considerations when electing that program pathway for certain children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 410.1209—Requesting Specific Consent From ORR Regarding Custody Proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for stakeholders to request ORR consent related to juvenile-custody proceedings involving children in ORR custody.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains statutory limits on state juvenile court jurisdiction and ORR's role in consenting to such proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 410.1210—Post-Release Services
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR's obligations or expectations to provide follow-up/post-release services after a child is released to a sponsor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes safety-and-well-being follow-up calls (currently 30 days) and describes authority to provide or coordinate services for children with ongoing needs (mental health, special needs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 410.1300—Purpose of Subpart D (Minimum Standards and Required Services)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains the purpose to codify minimum standards and required services for care provider facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to ensure safety, well-being, and uniform compliance with FSA, statutes, and existing ORR policy across facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 410.1301—Applicability of This Subpart
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies which facilities and programs the minimum standards apply to (standard programs, with exceptions noted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States applicability to care provider facilities receiving ORR funding and notes exceptions for non-standard or emergency facilities where tailored standards apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 410.1302—Minimum Standards Applicable to Standard Programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets the baseline minimum standards that standard programs must meet to provide care (education, health, safety, supervision, living standards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References Exhibit 1 of the FSA and ORR policy guide standards; expects compliance with state licensing and ORR-specific requirements; notes allowable cost treatment under CFR 75.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 410.1303—Reporting, Monitoring, Quality Control, and Recordkeeping Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for reporting data, monitoring facility performance, quality control processes, and maintaining records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Care providers must report required data to ORR (see subpart F), maintain case files and post-release records, allow monitoring and audits, and comply with recordkeeping timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 410.1304—Behavior Management and Prohibition on Seclusion and Restraint
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards governing behavior management techniques and an explicit prohibition on seclusion and certain restraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits seclusion and restricts use of restraint; requires positive behavior supports, de-escalation, trauma-informed approaches, and documentation/reporting of behavioral incidents per ORR policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 410.1305—Staff, Training, and Case Manager Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum qualifications, staffing ratios, training requirements, and case manager duties for personnel at care provider facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires staff training in trauma-informed care, child welfare, cultural competency, language access, and other topic areas; staffing levels must support safe care and case management functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 410.1306—Language Access Services
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements to provide language access services to ensure children can communicate and access services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Care providers must provide interpretation and translation appropriate to children's needs and ensure meaningful access to services, consistent with Title VI and other civil rights obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 410.1307—Healthcare Services
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards requiring access to timely and comprehensive healthcare and reproductive-health information/services where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires access to medical, dental, mental health care; timely pregnancy-related services and information consistent with applicable guidance and settlements (e.g., Garza); adherence to health/dietary guidelines and relevant CFR parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 410.1308—Child Advocates
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for the provision of child advocates to effectively advocate for the best interests of the child.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Child advocates must have access to necessary materials to advocate; ORR references statutory requirements (8 U.S.C. 1232(c)(6)(A)) and GAO/ORR guidance on program effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 410.1309—Legal Services
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR proposes, to the greatest extent practicable and subject to available resources, that all unaccompanied children who are or have been in ORR care have access to legal advice and representation in immigration matters funded by ORR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies access to counsel is a 'privilege' under statute (not a regulatory 'right'); ORR intends to expand legal services availability, fund legal assistance in certain circumstances, and provide legal information consistent with FSA paragraph A.14.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 410.1310—Psychotropic Medications
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards governing assessment, prescription, monitoring, and oversight of psychotropic medication use for children in care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires clinical review and safeguards before prescribing psychotropic medications, informed consent/assent practices, documentation, and periodic review; aligns with trauma-informed care principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 410.1311—Unaccompanied Children With Disabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements to identify, accommodate, and provide services to children with disabilities in ORR care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Care providers must ensure accessibility, individualized supports, special education services where applicable, and reasonable modifications consistent with federal disability law and ORR policy guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart E—Transportation of an Unaccompanied Child (Section 410.1400–410.1401)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and requirements for safe transportation of children while in ORR care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR requires safe transport protocols, provider responsibilities during transit, medical/behavioral safeguards, staff training for transport, and documentation of transport arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart F—Data and Reporting Requirements (Section 410.1500–410.1501)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for reporting information so ORR may compile and maintain statistical and other data on unaccompanied children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies data elements, reporting frequency, privacy protections, and uses of data for program oversight and policy making; links to reporting obligations in other CFR parts and ORR policy guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart G—Transfers (Section 410.1600–410.1601)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and policies regarding transfer of unaccompanied children within the ORR care provider facility network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes criteria for intra-network transfers, notification requirements, continuity of care and records transfer, and limits on transfers consistent with best interests and least restrictive setting principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart H—Age Determinations (Sections 410.1700–410.1704)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines for conducting age determinations, applicability, evidence considered, and treatment of individuals who appear to be adults.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies procedures, documentation, use of available credible evidence, privacy protections, reliance on ORR Policy Guide instructions, and special handling when the individual appears to be an adult.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart I—Emergency and Influx Operations (Sections 410.1800–410.1802)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contingency planning and procedures during an emergency or influx; minimum and placement standards specific to emergency/influx facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires contingency plans, surge staffing and facility standards, modified placement and supervision protocols for influx facilities, and minimum protections to ensure child safety even under emergency conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart J—Availability of Review of Certain ORR Decisions (Sections 410.1900–410.1903)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides for availability of administrative review of certain ORR decisions including restrictive placement case reviews, placement review panels, and risk determination hearings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes hearing/review processes, roles of review bodies, timetables, and the relationship between hearing findings and ORR placement/release decisions (e.g., hearings inform ORR but may not compel release).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart K—UC Office of the Ombuds (Sections 410.2000–410.2004)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposes establishment, organization, scope, responsibilities, and confidentiality standards for a UC Office of the Ombuds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ombuds will be independent, impartial, confidential public official (per USOA standards and ACUS report); responsibilities include receiving/investigating complaints, making findings/recommendations, publishing reports, and staffing/annual cost estimates provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key Principles of an Office of the Ombuds
rubrics_metrics.description: Articulates principles that an ombuds office should follow: independence, impartiality, confidentiality, authority to receive and informally address complaints, and ability to make findings/recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References Standards Committee of United States Ombudsman Association and ACUS reports as models; expects ombuds to align with best practices for government ombudsmen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Participation—General Encouragement
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR encourages all interested parties to submit written comments, views, and data on all aspects of the proposed rule, including economic, environmental, or federalism effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States ORR will consider all comments and may change the rule based on comments; all submitted comments will be posted to regulations.gov (subject to redaction policies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Participation—Submitting Comments (Instructions and Criteria for Useful Comments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on how to submit comments that will provide the most assistance to ORR: reference specific portions of the proposed rule, explain reasons for recommended changes, and include supporting data, information, or authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requesters should indicate specific sections to which each comment applies, provide reasons and evidence, use only one submission method (online OR email), follow regs.gov submission steps (insert docket number, 'Comment Now!', etc.), and understand posting/redaction practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Participation—Viewing Comments and Documents (Docket Access)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions to view comments and docket documents via regulations.gov (insert docket '0970-AC93', 'Open Docket Folder', 'View Comment' or 'View All').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals without internet access can arrange alternative viewing via ORR contact; users can sign up for email alerts; postings may be delayed pending agency approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Participation—Privacy Act and Redaction Notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice that comments will be posted without change to regulations.gov and that personal information included in comments may be publicly searchable; ORR may redact certain content before posting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies categories subject to redaction (threats, hate speech, profanity, graphic images, personally identifiable information about third parties) and points to the regs.gov 'Privacy and Security Notice'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Summary—Codification to Implement FSA and Statute
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR proposes to codify requirements consistent with HSA, TVPRA, and the substantive protections of the Flores Settlement Agreement as they pertain to ORR's responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes purpose to create uniform standards, ensure safety/well-being, and enhance transparency; notes some costs and estimated fiscal impacts (e.g., ombuds office costs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Least Restrictive Setting Principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandates placement of minors in the 'least restrictive setting appropriate to the minor's age and special needs.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a central tenet drawn from the FSA and reflected throughout placement and restrictive-placement criteria; exceptions only when necessary for safety, treatment, or other statutory reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of Priority for Release Sponsors (FSA-derived)
rubrics_metrics.description: When release is appropriate, ORR follows priority: parent, legal guardian, adult relative, another adult designated by parent/guardian capable and willing to care for the minor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no sponsor available, placement at state-licensed care provider facility; sponsor priority guides release screening and home-study triggers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Impact & Cost Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR analyzes baseline costs, estimated additional costs (legal services expansion, risk determination hearing process, ombuds office), and funding mechanisms including allowable costs under 45 CFR 75.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains anticipated limited additional costs, eligibility for supplemental funds, and ORR's estimate of annual ombuds office cost (~$1,718,529).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with Other Laws and Protections (Civil Rights, Education, Federalism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires compliance with other federal laws (Title VI, Equal Educational Opportunity Act, state education access rules, federalism considerations, civil rights obligations) in provision of services to children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include prohibitions on school enrollment discrimination, limits on documentation requirements, and coordination with DOJ/ED guidance on school enrollment rights for children regardless of immigration status.
